skill.name: scaffolding-openai-agents
skill.description: Guides developers through building OpenAI Agents SDK applications with async runners, tools, handoffs, guardrails, and FastAPI integration.
skill.summary: Scaffold OpenAI Agents SDK projects with practical patterns for tools, routing, guardrails, streaming, and web APIs.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms one high-risk unsafe code example: a function tool calls eval() on a model or user-controlled expression. Most other static findings are false positives from markdown fences, placeholder API key setup, benign verification text, or documentation links; one outbound weather example is kept as a low-risk network concern.

remediation.issue: The calculate tool uses eval() on an expression argument.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval() with a safe parser, a constrained arithmetic library, or explicit operation handling before publication.

remediation.issue: The weather tool sends caller-provided city text to a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Validate and encode the city value, document the outbound request, and prefer a configurable trusted weather API endpoint.

content.value_statement: Developers need repeatable examples for building agent workflows without starting from blank files. This skill provides practical OpenAI Agents SDK patterns for tools, handoffs, guardrails, streaming, and FastAPI integration.
actual_capabilities: Shows basic Agent and Runner patterns for async, sync, and streaming execution.
Demonstrates function tools, async tools, and Pydantic typed tool inputs.
Explains multi-agent handoffs and agents-as-tools orchestration.
Provides input and output guardrail examples for tutoring workflows.
Outlines FastAPI endpoints for standard and streamed agent responses.
Includes a verification script that checks required skill sections.
limitations: Focuses on OpenAI Agents SDK and does not cover LangChain or raw OpenAI API usage.
Contains tutorial snippets that require security review before production use.
Does not provide a complete packaged application or deployment pipeline.
Assumes Python familiarity and access to an OpenAI API key.

use_cases.title: Create a tutoring agent
use_cases.description: Use the examples to build a Python tutor with guardrails, conversation history, and specialist handoffs.

use_cases.title: Prototype tool-calling workflows
use_cases.description: Adapt the function tool patterns to connect agents with calculators, search tools, or external services.

use_cases.title: Add agents to a web API
use_cases.description: Use the FastAPI examples to expose agent responses through standard and streaming endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a first OpenAI Agents SDK script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to scaffold a simple OpenAI Agents SDK assistant that answers Python questions with async Runner.run.

prompt_templates.title: Add safe tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design function tools for my agent. Include typed inputs, validation, and safe alternatives to dynamic code execution.

prompt_templates.title: Route across specialists
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a triage agent that routes requests to research, writing, and debugging specialists using handoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Ship through FastAPI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add FastAPI endpoints for my agent, including a normal response endpoint and a streaming response endpoint.

output_examples.input: Build a Python tutor agent with conversation history.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with an Agent definition, async Runner.run usage, message history handling, and a verification step.

output_examples.input: Add specialist handoffs for debugging and practice exercises.
output: A triage design with named specialist agents.
A routing description for each specialist.
A test prompt to confirm the handoff path.

output_examples.input: Expose the agent through FastAPI with streaming.
output_examples.output: Endpoint guidance for request models, normal responses, streaming responses, and error handling boundaries.

best_practices: Replace tutorial shortcuts with validated, production-safe implementations before deployment.
Use typed inputs and guardrails when tools receive model or user-controlled data.
Test each handoff and tool path with realistic prompts before connecting external services.
anti_patterns: Do not copy the eval() calculator example into production code.
Do not expose agent tools that call external services without validation and user awareness.
Do not use this skill for non-SDK frameworks when the project already depends on another agent library.

faq.question: What framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets the OpenAI Agents SDK for Python, especially Agent, Runner, tools, handoffs, guardrails, and streaming.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code can use the skill as guidance while editing Python agent projects or creating examples.

faq.question: Does it create a complete production app?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and snippets that need project-specific integration, testing, and security hardening.

faq.question: Are the tool examples safe for production?
faq.answer: Not all of them. The calculator example uses eval() and must be replaced with a safe implementation.

faq.question: Does it support streaming responses?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Runner.run_streamed examples and a FastAPI streaming endpoint pattern.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when the project uses raw API calls, LangChain, or another framework instead of the OpenAI Agents SDK.
